plan.title: No destination yet: no pushing for one, and the plan still locks

context.text: 20 min is about all I've got before I fall asleep lol
Twenty it is. Do you track your reading anywhere, like Goodreads or a notes app?

transcript.text: nope, no app. and no idea what I'm aiming for yet tbh, I just want to read more

No worries, "just read more" is a solid place to start. Here's the plan:

• Today's step: read Atomic Habits in bed for 20 minutes, from wherever you are (or page 1)
• When: 9 pm, every day
• Proof: a short voice note recapping what you read, in your own words
• Why: 20 minutes is short enough to finish before you get sleepy, and the book is already on your nightstand
• Easy alternative: if talking feels like a lot, tell me and we'll tweak how you show it

Each day shapes the next step, and a destination can come later once you see what you like. I'll text you around 9 to get you set.

What do you think?
Love it, Jordan. Twenty minutes with Atomic Habits at 9 tonight. Are you officially committing to this?
Locked in, Jordan. LFG! 📚 Day 1 is tonight at 9 pm: 20 minutes of Atomic Habits in bed, then a quick voice note telling me what you read.

checks.reason: Plan presentation runs about 9 short lines including the bullets, slightly over the roughly 8-line allowance.
Uses plain bullets with no markdown, hashtags or filler.
Warm and sincere, but calm rather than pushy-level energy; no emoji used.
Uses only what Jordan said (Atomic Habits, nightstand, 9 pm, 20 minutes) plus a voice-note proof suggestion.
Day 1 gives what (Atomic Habits), where (in bed), when (9 pm) and how long (20 minutes).
Plain conversational wording with no markdown or filler.
Warm, specific and not overfamiliar; no emoji.
Refers back to the agreed 20 minutes and Atomic Habits at 9 tonight without invented facts.
Two sentences confirming the lock and day 1.
No markdown or filler; the single emoji is used as punctuation.
Hype line 'LFG!' fits a locked commitment and stays warm.
Day 1 states what, where, when, how long and the voice-note proof.
After locking, the text carries the day 1 next move.

conversation.reason: No extra plan questions were asked; the plan went straight to the lock.
Concrete five-line plan with what, how much, where, when and a voice-note proof that fits a non-app user.
Shows day 1, schedule, proof and a one-line progression note with no list of future steps.
Did not re-ask the destination; only a light note that one can come later, and the plan locked smoothly.
After 'looks good' it asked in natural words whether Jordan is committing; the ask feels real.
Day 1 is set for tonight at 9 pm.
Plan shown as a bullet list ending with the single question 'What do you think?'.
Matches the expected flow: no repeat destination ask, full day 1 plan, natural commitment ask, and a clean lock.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the no-destination case well: it skipped re-asking, presented a concrete voice-note plan, asked for commitment naturally and locked with no friction. The only soft spot is that the plan text runs slightly long and its energy is a bit calmer than the pushy default.
